stage: diagnostic studies, not active game assets
side_prompt: Repair the referenced Dagna WALK ANIMATION study. Make a transparent spritesheet of exactly FOUR complete figures in ONE horizontal row, all facing RIGHT in exact side profile. Preserve adult compact dwarf identity, chestnut wavy hair, red bodice, cream short sleeves, apron, weighty boots, bold hand-painted contours. This is a slow grounded WALK not march/run. Keep body scale, face, hair length and head placement consistent across four equal cells with generous margins. Physical NEAR leg always wears RED boot, FAR leg always BLUE; colors identify limbs, never exchange at hips. Frame1: NEAR red leg extends FORWARD heel on ground to the right; FAR blue leg extends BACK toe on ground to left. NEAR arm swings BACK, FAR arm forward. Frame2: NEAR red leg VERTICAL under pelvis bearing weight; FAR blue knee bends and foot passes just behind supporting red ankle, blue toe lifted slightly. NEAR arm at side. Frame3: FAR BLUE leg extends FORWARD heel on ground to right, NEAR RED leg extends BACK toe touching ground to left, with red leg drawn IN FRONT where silhouettes cross. NEAR arm swings FORWARD and FAR arm BACK, clearly reversing frame1. Frame4: FAR BLUE leg VERTICAL under pelvis bearing weight; NEAR RED knee bent slightly FORWARD with red ankle passing just in front of blue support ankle, toe lifted slightly. NEAR arm at side. Contact1 and contact3 have equal wide stride but opposite physical legs. Passing2 and passing4 are narrow silhouettes, not kicking/marching. Feet on identical baseline, pelvis above same column center; tiny natural rise on passing. No weapons, no text, no floor shadows. Exactly four whole painted drawings with both arms and both legs anatomically attached; no collage.
side_arm_repair: Preserve all poses. Reverse only third figure's arms so near arm swings forward and far arm back.
other_views_prompt: Create the OTHER THREE CAMERA VIEWS of Dagna's four-key walk cycle. Image1 is corrected side-walk timing authority; image2 is appearance/turnaround reference ONLY (its walk poses are wrong, do NOT copy them). Output exactly FOUR columns x THREE rows, 12 whole drawings. Every figure inside equal cell with generous transparent margin. Row1 all four face straight TOWARD viewer. Row2 all four face diagonally AWAY and RIGHT (rear 3/4). Row3 all four face straight AWAY. Keep same dwarf adult woman, chestnut waves, red bodice/skirt, cream short sleeves/apron, brown wrist cuffs; compact powerful body and short legs, bold outlined painting readable at62px. Physical LEFT boot RED and RIGHT boot BLUE for diagnostic only. Every row is same sequential cycle: col1 LEFT RED heel reaches FORWARD in travel direction, right blue toe trails BACK; right arm forward left arm back. Col2 LEFT RED is planted below pelvis, RIGHT BLUE foot swings through beside it with toe just above ground, legs almost overlap. Col3 RIGHT BLUE heel reaches FORWARD in travel direction, LEFT RED toe trails BACK; LEFT arm forward RIGHT arm back. Col4 RIGHT BLUE planted below pelvis, LEFT RED foot swings through with toe lifted, legs almost overlap. In front row RED is on viewer RIGHT and BLUE on viewer LEFT throughout, so col1 red boot appears lower/larger, col3 BLUE appears lower/larger. In back row RED is on viewer LEFT and BLUE on viewer RIGHT throughout: col1 RED farther away/higher and BLUE trailing nearest/lower heel, col3 BLUE farther away/higher and RED trailing nearest/lower heel. Never change which side each leg attaches to. Equal stride length in contact columns1/3. Passing2/4 have narrow stance, NO high marching knees. Opposite arm swing col1 vs3. Hair stable, no turn within each row. Same ground baseline and body proportions across frames. No text, shadow, terrain, grid, or props. Transparent background.

review.side: Native four-frame capture reviewed at 62px and enlarged: red contact, blue passing, blue contact, red passing, with opposing arms. Diagnostic only; no production approval.
review.other_views: Rejected: boot colors change anatomical sides and arms repeat. No activation.
